title: Groups and periods: reading the periodic table
examples: What is the difference between a group and a period?
Why are elements in a group alike?
Where are the metals on the periodic table?

explain.say: The periodic table looks like a big grid of boxes. But it is really a clever map, where every row and column means something. Look at the board. You can see one column and one row of elements.

draw.text: Groups and periods: reading the periodic table

explain.say: See the first group lit up? A column going down is called a group. Lithium, sodium and potassium are all in group 1. They are all soft, shiny metals that fizz in water. What do you think they have in common inside?

Look at the reasons on the board. Every group 1 atom has one electron in its outer shell, and outer electrons do the reacting. So the group number tells you the outer electrons! How many would a group 7 atom have?

draw.name: x-why
draw.question: Why are elements in a group alike?

because.label: Same outer electrons
because.ask: Why are elements in a group alike?

because.label: Same reactions
because.note: So they behave in similar ways.

draw.answer: Same number of outer electrons, so similar reactions

explain.say: Seven! Now look at the row. A row going across is called a period. Sodium, magnesium, aluminium and the rest are in period 3, because their atoms all have 3 shells. Metals sit on the left, non-metals on the right. Can you spot the metals in this row?

Sodium, magnesium and aluminium! Well done. Here you can compare them: groups are families with the same outer electrons; periods are rows with the same number of shells. Wow: Mendeleev used these patterns in 1869 to predict elements nobody had found yet.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Groups are families; periods are rows

faq.q: What is a group in the periodic table?
faq.a: A group is a column. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons, so they react in similar ways.

faq.q: What is a period in the periodic table?
faq.a: A period is a row. Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.

faq.q: Why are elements in a group alike?
faq.a: They have the same number of electrons in their outer shell, and the outer electrons decide how an atom reacts.
asks: Why do group 1 metals behave the same?

faq.q: Where are the metals on the periodic table?
faq.a: Metals are on the left and in the middle, which is most of the table. Non-metals are on the right, with a zigzag staircase line between them.
asks: Where are non-metals on the periodic table?

faq.q: How many groups and periods are there?
faq.a: The modern periodic table has 18 groups and 7 periods.
asks: How many rows and columns does the periodic table have?

facts: The modern periodic table has 18 groups (columns) and 7 periods (rows).
Dmitri Mendeleev published his periodic table in 1869 and left gaps for undiscovered elements such as gallium and germanium.

quiz.say: Magnesium is 2, 8, 2. Which group and period is it in?
quiz.show: Magnesium is 2, 8, 2. Which group and period is it in?
quiz.why: 2 outer electrons means group 2; 3 shells means period 3.

wrong.0: The outer electrons give the group and the shells give the period, not the other way round.
wrong.1: It has 2 outer electrons and 3 shells.

quiz.say: Why do sodium and potassium react in similar ways?
quiz.show: Why do sodium and potassium react in similar ways?
quiz.why: They are both in group 1, with one outer electron.

wrong.0: Potassium is in period 4; they share a group, not a period.
wrong.2: Their masses are different: about 23 and 39.
